question: What a unit draws each day and what changes a brigade from one day to the next without a battle: supplies and fuel, troop rotation, the reinforcement share and the upgrade share.

addresses.name: CSubUnit::CanReinforce
addresses.no_signature: the brigade arrives in esi and nothing is on the stack; a bool comes back in al
addresses.comment: **Whether a brigade, ship or wing is in a state to be brought back to strength.** The brigade in esi, a bool in al, bare `ret`s at 0x5AC1E3 and 0x5AC2AC. False unless strength (+0x5C) is below GetMaxStrength(0, 0), that maximum is positive and the brigade is in a unit (+0xB0). Then false for a land unit (the unit's slot 15) with a combat (unit +0x11C > 0), for any unit that is retreating (unit +0x158), and for a land unit that is being carried - the unit's slot 9 answers an object whose +0x300 or +0x304 is set. Last, for a ship (the brigade's own slot 10) false unless the unit's province's info byte +0x22 is set: **a ship is reinforced only in a province that is land, which is to say in port.** One caller, CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute at 0x51BF9C. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: `mov edi,[esi+0x5c]`; `push 0; push 0; ...; call [vftable+0x30]`; `cmp edi,[eax]; jl`; second call and `cmp dword ptr [eax],0; jle`; `cmp dword ptr [esi+0xb0],0; je`; `call [unit vftable+0x3c]` then `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x11c],0; jg`; `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x158],0; jne`; two `call [unit vftable+0x24]` each followed by `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x300],0` and `[eax+0x304]`; `call [vftable+0x28]` then `mov edx,[ecx+0x130]; mov eax,[edx+0xd4]; cmp byte ptr [eax+0x22],0; je`; `mov al,1`. Wrong if any of the false exits is in fact the true one: every one of them jumps to 0x5AC1DE, which is `xor al,al`.

addresses.name: CDistributeSupply::GetNeeded
addresses.comment: **Slot 3: the supply slider's need**, a 48.15 fixed point through the out pointer, `ret 4`. supplies = the country's unit_demand.supplies (+0xA48) + traded_away.supplies (+0x7E4) - tribute_sent.supplies (+0x928) - traded_for.supplies (+0x874) - tribute_received.supplies (+0x904), each turned from thousandths into fixed 15; zero where that is not positive. Otherwise it is divided by IC_TO_SUPPLIES (economy +0x10) x (1 + technology_status->supply_production_bonus (+0x9C) + MODIFIER_GLOBAL_SUPPLIES) - exactly what CDistributeSupply::GetSuppliesMade multiplies an allocation by. So the need is **the IC that would make the supplies the country's units asked for today**. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: `mov ebx,[ecx+0x18]`; five loads `[ebx+0xa48]`, `[ebx+0x904]`, `[ebx+0x874]`, `[ebx+0x7e4]`, `[ebx+0x928]`, each followed by `shld edx,eax,0x1e; shl eax,0x1e` and a divide by 0x1F40000; `sub esi,eax` for +0x928, `sub esi,[esp+0x10]` (+0x874), `sub esi,[esp+0x18]` (+0x904), `add esi,[esp+0x20]` (+0xA48); `mov ecx,[eax+0x10]` off defines +0x9C; `mov eax,[edx+0x9c]` off +0xDF8 and `mov ecx,[ecx+0xd8]` off +0xDA8, added; `add ebx,0x8000`; a final __alldiv; `ret 4`. vtable.py --holding 0x51B660 answers CDistributeSupply slot 3 and nothing else.

addresses.name: CUnit::CUnit
addresses.no_signature: the body was not read to its return, so neither the arguments nor the cleanup is known
addresses.comment: **CUnit's constructor.** Not read through; recorded for what a unit starts with, which three readings depend on. At 0x5B5410 it writes the word 0x0100 to +0xA4 and the byte 1 to +0xA6: **priority off, upgrades on, reinforcement on**. At 0x5B52A1 it writes 1000 to both supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100), having zeroed them at 0x5B5154, so a unit that has never drawn counts as fully supplied - which is what the first day's troop rotation sees. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 8.
addresses.evidence: image.functionStart(0x5B5154) answers 0x5B5010. `mov word ptr [edi+0xa4],0x100` and `mov byte ptr [edi+0xa6],1` at 0x5B5410 and 0x5B5419; `mov eax,0x3e8; mov [edi+0xfc],eax; mov [edi+0x100],eax` at 0x5B529C. That it is the constructor rests on the run of zeroing stores over the whole object from +0x58 to +0x2B0 and on the fields it initialises; its arguments and its `ret` were not read, which is why this is `inferred` and carries no signature.

addresses.name: g_ReinforcementCrowdingFloor
addresses.comment: 250, a quarter: the floor of the float 250.5 at 0x160A688, written once at startup by the initialiser at 0xCB846B. The least CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute will slow a fleet's or an air unit's reinforcement for a crowded base (0x51BF70). No define moves it.
addresses.evidence: staticconst over 0x1A87710: one writer, `mov dword ptr [0x1a87710],eax` at 0xCB846B after `movss xmm0,[0x160a688]; floorf; _ftol2_sse`; one reader, `mov ecx,[0x1a87710]; cmp eax,ecx; jge` at 0x51BF70.

addresses.name: g_ReinforcementDailyShare
addresses.comment: 500, a half: the floor of the float 500.5 at 0x160A5E8, written once at startup at 0xCB858B. Two readers. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute multiplies a thirtieth of a brigade's full strength by it (0x51C150), so a day at full speed brings back a sixtieth; CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute divides it by the levels a brigade is behind (0x51D3A1), so a day of one technology costs half the brigade's price over all its technologies. No define moves it.
addresses.evidence: staticconst over 0x1A87730: one writer at 0xCB858B off the float 500.5; `imul dword ptr [0x1a87730]` at 0x51C150 and `mov eax,[0x1a87730]` at 0x51D3A1.

addresses.name: g_UpgradeLeastRate
addresses.comment: 1, a thousandth: the floor of the float 1.5 at 0x17179AC, written once at startup at 0xCB82BB. The least a day moves one level of one technology on in CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute, however long the brigade takes to build (0x51D2C5). No define moves it.

addresses.name: CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute(CDistributeReinforcement* this, CFixedPoint* result@stack:4, __int64 available@stack:8, bool flag@stack:16)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 0, read through**: 0x51BA60 to the `ret 0x10` at 0x51C669. The reinforcement slider spending what it has been allocated, and where the manpower tooltip's two numbers come from. `this + 0x18` is the country throughout.

budget = base_percentage x available x factor in thousandths; free = the same share of lend_lease_ic (+0x608). It zeroes CCountry +0xA98, +0xA9C and +0xAA0, then builds a list: the country's units (+0xBAC) less those with an expeditionary owner, then its second unit list (+0xBBC), each needing reinforcements_active (+0xA6), **a unit with +0xA4 set going to the front**. For a fleet or an air unit a crowding factor is worked out from its base - the base's room over the brigades stationed there, clamped to 250..1000 (g_ReinforcementCrowdingFloor).

Per brigade that passes CSubUnit::CanReinforce: max = GetMaxStrength(0,0); share = (max - strength) x 1000 / max, **and a share of zero skips the brigade** - it is not touched until it is short by a thousandth of what it may have. speed = (1000 + REINFORCEMENT_BONUS) x (1000 + UNIT_REPAIR) x crowding x the unit's supply_received_percentage; a day's gain = speed x (definition max_strength / 30) x g_ReinforcementDailyShare, **a sixtieth of full strength at full speed**. The men it takes are the gain's share of build_cost_manpower, and where the country has fewer the gain is cut to what it has. ic = max(BuildCostIC, 1.000) x repair_cost_multiplier (+0x104), x max(1, -5 x RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE) for a reserve - **a cost by the day, with no term in how much is brought back**. Where the gain would overfill the brigade, what is added is **missing x 1000 / speed** and ic and the men are scaled to that.

Only while budget > 0: resources are charged for ic less what is left of `free`, the strength is raised and clamped, the experience becomes (1 - g) x old + g x UNIT_START_EXPERIENCE where g is the share of full strength added (and PRIDE_BONUS_EXP is added to the old figure of a ship that is the pride - read, not understood), the manpower comes off the pool, and **the whole ic comes off the budget afterwards, so the share overspends by one brigade**. ic and the manpower needed are added to the counters whether or not anything was spent, which is what makes +0xA98 the slider's need. It ignores the flag and returns zero.

**The stack arguments are three, not one**: a hidden return pointer at [ebp+8], the allocation as a 64-bit fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15> across [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10], and a byte flag at [ebp+0x14]. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 4, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md for the counters.
addresses.evidence: Read from the function's own entry, stack slots tracked through every pending push. `cmp byte ptr [edi+0xa6],0; je` and `cmp byte ptr [edi+0xa4],0` choosing between the two node shapes (link at +8 for the front, at +4 for the back); `call 0x5ac1c0; test al,al; je`; `test eax,eax; jle 0x51c612` on the share at 0x51C067; `mov eax,[ecx+0x2b0]; add eax,0x3e8` (86) and `[esi+0x1a8]` (53); `imul dword ptr [edx+0xfc]`; the divide by 30000 as `imul 0x45e7b273; sar edx,0xd`; `imul dword ptr [0x1a87730]`; `mov eax,[edx+0xf8]; cmp eax,0x3e8; jge`; `cmp byte ptr [ebx+0xa4],0; je` before `imul dword ptr [esp+0x58]`; `imul dword ptr [edx+0x104]`; `lea edx,[edi+eax]; cmp edx,ecx; jl 0x51c445`; `cmp dword ptr [esp+0x4c],0; jle 0x51c5f1`. **Checked against five savegames of one game**: a regular German brigade of 30 loses 0.002 a day and is 0.004 short after two days with 31 IC in the share, 0.013-0.014 short a month on; a reserve of 15 is always half as far short. Wrong if a brigade under a thousandth short is ever seen topped up.
addresses.revises: the comment described the three counters and the argument layout; the whole body is now read and the comment says what a day does, including the thousandth below which a brigade is skipped. Signature and confidence unchanged

addresses.name: CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute
addresses.signature: CFixedPoint* __thiscall CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute(CDistributeUpgrade* this, CFixedPoint* out@stack:4, __int64 available@stack:8, bool flag@stack:16)
addresses.comment:
**Slot 0, read through**: 0x51CE60 to the `ret 0x10` at 0x51D5B5. budget = base_percentage x available x factor in thousandths; free = the same share of lend_lease_ic. It zeroes its own +0x20 (an __int64, the count of brigades upgrading in fixed 15, which the tooltip prints as UNITS) and CCountry +0xAA4, upgrade_cost. The list is the country's second unit list (+0xBBC) and then its own units (+0xBAC) less those with an expeditionary owner, each needing upgrade_active (+0xA5), a unit with +0xA4 set going to the front.

For every node of every brigade's `technologies` whose technology has canUpgrade (+0x314) and whose level is below the country's level_by_technology (or, for a government in exile, the first member of its faction's if higher): days = CCountry::GetBuildTime(country, the brigade's definition, 0); rate = max(1000000 / (days x 1000) x 2, g_UpgradeLeastRate) x the SHIP_/AIR_/LAND_UPGRADE_SPEED_MOD define, **thousandths of a level a day**. cost = BuildCostIC x (1000 + build_cost_by_unit_type - GetCategoryBuildDiscount) / 1000, x (1000 + RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE) / 1000 for a reserve; daily = cost / the brigade's technology count x g_ReinforcementDailyShare / levels behind. **A technology whose `change` (+0x288) is clear - a doctrine - costs nothing and moves a whole level a day.** Where daily is more than the budget left, the progress is budget x 2 x rate / 1000 and the rest of the budget is paid; after that nothing more moves. progress is added to the node's +0x8; at 1000 it goes back to zero and the level goes up one, and after the brigade's last technology CUnit::RebuildDefinition is called on its unit. upgrade_cost takes every `daily`, spent or not - the slider's need. Resources are charged once at the end for what was spent less `free`. It ignores the flag and returns zero.

**Checked against a savegame two days in**: with the save's shares and the laws the day ran under, two days of this reproduce the `{level progress}` pair on all 1,469 of Germany's technology lines, including the wing the share ran out on (0.008 where its neighbours have 0.020) and the three after it with nothing. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Read from the function's own entry. `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x314],0; je`; `mov eax,[eax+0x244]` indexing `[ecx+0x218]`; `cmp ecx,[edx+4]; jle`; `call CCountry::GetBuildTime`; `mov eax,0xf4240; cdq; idiv ecx` then x 0x7D0 / 1000; `cmp esi,eax; cmovl esi,eax` against the local holding [0x1A8776C]; the three defines at military +0x2AC, +0x2B0, +0x2B4 chosen by the brigade's slots 10 and 11; `mov ecx,[eax+0xf8]`; `call CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount`; `mov esi,[ecx+0x8c]; imul esi,esi,0x3e8` (the technology count); `mov eax,[0x1a87730]`; `cmp byte ptr [edx+0x288],0; jne` over `xor edi,edi; mov esi,0x3e8`; `cmp edi,ebx; jle` over the x 0x7D0 partial; `add [eax+8],esi; cmp dword ptr [eax+8],0x3e8; jl`; `inc dword ptr [eax+4]`; `add [eax+0xaa4],edi`; `add dword ptr [esi+0x20],0x8000`; `call CUnit::RebuildDefinition`; `call CCountry::ConsumeIcResources` at 0x51D56E. Wrong if a brigade's progress in a later save is not a whole number of days of its rate.
addresses.revises: was `inferred` and 'not read line by line', a list of what it calls; now read through and `confirmed`. The signature is unchanged

addresses.name: CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount(int* out@ESI, CCountry* country@stack:4, CTechnologyCategory* category@stack:8)
addresses.comment:
The discount a technology category earns, in thousandths, which a build cost is scaled by as (1000 - this) and a build time takes off its first factor. Takes the country's ability in that category - its own level at +0x698, or the sharer's if a tag at +0x6A8 names one with a higher level, the same lookup GetAbility makes - floors it at 0 and measures it against 5.000. Below that the result is negative and the cost goes up, at 100 a point. Above it, **a surplus of more than one point is first put through FixedPointSqrt** (0x69CEC0, the rough square root research uses for the same purpose), and what comes out is worth 50 a point. Then it adds the country's INDUSTRIAL_EFFICIENCY modifier (74) and CTechnologyStatus +0x94 - what the technology key `ic_efficiency` adds up to - and caps the whole at 990, so at most 99% off. The name is BiceLib's.

**The out pointer travels in ESI, not on the stack** - that is the whole of why the recorded signature wanted ret 12 and the function does ret 8. Only two things are pushed, the country and the category; ESI is never written in the body, only read (every store is `mov [esi], ...`), and the return is `mov eax, esi` at 0x4E1BCA. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: `add dword ptr [esi],0xffffec78; mov eax,[esi]; jns` - the negative arm is `imul dword ptr [ebp-4]` with the local holding floor(100.5f); the other is `cmp eax,0x3e8; jle` over `push ecx; ...; call 0xa9cec0` and then `imul dword ptr [ebp+8]` with floor(50.5f); `mov eax,[eax+0x250]; add eax,[edx+0x94]`; the cap is the local holding floor(990.5f). **The +0x94 term is measured**: with Germany's four levels of industral_efficiency at `ic_efficiency = 0.025`, two days of CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute reproduce a savegame on all 1,469 of its technology lines; without it every build time is a tenth long and the share runs out four wings early.
addresses.revises: the comment said a surplus over 5 was worth 50 a point 'with everything past 1.000 halved first'. It is put through FixedPointSqrt, whose first guess is the halving; and the +0x94 term is now tied to the `ic_efficiency` key. Signature unchanged

addresses.name: CUnit::SupplyConsumption
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall SupplyConsumption(CUnit* unit, int* out, bool withoutLeaders)
addresses.comment: Unit supply consumption in thousandths, written through out and returned in eax; ret 0xC. A potency starts at 1000; unless withoutLeaders, it takes the owner's SUPPLY_CONSUMPTION modifier (49), loses the army group leader's skill x 50 scaled by CommandReach - only where the unit stands in a province (+0x130) - and gains CommandEffect(unit, 2), floored at 0. Then per brigade: (potency + extra_consumption (+0xCC) x 10) x the definition's supply_consumption / 1000, and **unless the unit is naval** (slot 16) x strength x 1000 / the definition's max_strength / 1000. extra_consumption is the sum of every technology level the brigade holds, so each level is 1% more. Last, a land unit whose order answers 0x5A4 - a strategic redeployment - has the total x STRAT_REDEP_SUPPLY_MOD (military +0x1E8) / 1000, twice in Their Finest Hour. Both callers that move goods pass withoutLeaders = 0. **Measured**: with no leaders, the formula gives a capital's garrison to the thousandth in 38 of 65 savegame capitals. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [ebp+0x10],0; jne` over the potency block; `mov eax,[eax+0x188]; add eax,0x3e8`; the walk `cmp dword ptr [edi+0x1f4],1` / `mov edi,[edi+0x1e0]`; `cmp dword ptr [ebx+0x130],0; je`; `mov eax,[ecx+0x70]` off `[edi+0x12c]`; `push 2; ...; call CUnit::CommandEffect`; the float round of `[esi+0xcc]` and `imul dword ptr [0x1a8873c]`; `mov eax,[eax+0x110]`; `call [vftable+0x40]; test al,al; jne` over the strength scaling by `[ecx+0xec]`; `cmp eax,0x5a4; jne` over `mov ecx,[ecx+0x1e8]`.
addresses.revises: the comment was one line; it now carries the formula, names the define a redeploying army's supplies are multiplied by, and says the +0x130 test is the unit's province and not a leader. Signature unchanged

addresses.name: CRegiment::FuelConsumption
addresses.comment: Per regiment fuel consumption; the regiment in eax, ret 4. The same potency as the unit level one, reached through the regiment's own unit at +0xB0, and zero for a land regiment whose unit is on a strategic redeployment. **Unlike CUnit::FuelConsumption it scales by strength**: unless the regiment's slot 10 answers true, the figure is multiplied by strength x 1000 / the definition's max_strength. So the fuel a brigade shows for itself and the fuel its unit is charged are not the same sum; only the unit level routine is called by anything that moves goods.
addresses.evidence: `mov eax,[eax+0x114]; imul ebx`; `call [vftable+0x28]; test al,al; jne 0x5ad4d6` over `mov eax,[esi+0x5c]; mov esi,[ecx+0xec]` and the divide and multiply that follow; against 0x5BB8B0..0x5BB92D in the unit level routine, which has no read of +0x5C or +0xEC at all.
addresses.revises: adds that this routine scales by strength where the unit level one does not. Signature unchanged

addresses.name: CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel
addresses.comment:
The daily supply and fuel draw for one unit. Asks CUnit::SupplyConsumption (0x1BB560) and CUnit::FuelConsumption (0x1BB7A0), both with leaders, what the unit wants, takes what it can get, and writes CUnit::supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) as taken*1000/wanted. The country it bills is the expeditionary_owner (+0x28C) where CUnit +0x290 is set, the owner (+0x124) otherwise.

**Three callers**: CUnit::UpdateDaily at 0x5BB32C, after troop rotation and before attrition; RunCountryDailyPass at 0x4DB2C0, for each finished unit still in the deployment queue; and 0x678FD9, in the pass CInGameIdler::Enter runs as a game starts.

Two paths, chosen on g_CCurrentGameState +0xC9C. **> 0, the arcade path**: taken = min(wanted, CCountry::GetPool(payer)) straight out of the national stockpile, the payer's unit_demand (+0xA48, +0xA4C) takes what was asked, and nothing is booked to `usage`; a unit that wants nothing keeps the figure it had. **<= 0** walks the supply network - the unit's supply source province, its supply_depot_id (+0x48) into g_CMap +0x2200, and draws that province's pool.supplies (+0x164) and pool.fuel (+0x168) pro rata against the province's need (+0x24C, +0x250). On that path the amount taken is added to the supplying country's usage.supplies (+0x994) **only when the unit stands in that country's acting capital** (0x5BC197), which is why a save's `usage.supplies` is the capital's garrison plus the capital's throughput. Where the depot is controlled by another country a lend-lease conversion runs: the amount is scaled by a rate built from SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS and the pools at +0x7DC and +0x86C are credited.

**Fuel is only taken when the unit is moving** (movement_order_remaining_provinces_count > 0) **or is a fleet out of its own port** (naval and CUnit_IsAtOwnBase says no), on both paths; a land or air unit standing still burns none. The last act, for the player's own units only, is the out-of-supply marker on the counter. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, sections 1 and 3.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --callers 0x5BB950 answers 0x4DB2C0, 0x5BB32C and 0x678FD9. `cmp dword ptr [eax+0xc9c],0; jle 0x5bbc31`; on the arcade side `add [edi+0xa48],esi` and `add [edi+0xa4c],ecx` with no store to +0x994; `cmp dword ptr [ebx+0x140],0; jg` then `call [vftable+0x40]` and `call CUnit_IsAtOwnBase; test al,al; jne 0x5bc44a`; on the network side `call CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation; cmp eax,[edx+0x130]; jne` over `add [esi+0x994],ebx`.
addresses.revises: adds the three callers and where in the day they fall, the arcade path in full, and that usage.supplies counts only units standing in the capital. Signature unchanged

struct_fields.name: upgrade_prio
struct_fields.comment: **The unit's priority, for reinforcement as much as for upgrades**, saved as `is_prioritized`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute (0x51BC4F) and CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute (0x51CF96, 0x51D087) both read it for the same thing: a unit with it set joins the front of the list the share works through, the rest the back. The constructor clears it. The name is older than the second reader and is left as it is.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [edi+0xa4],0` choosing the node shape in both bodies; `mov word ptr [edi+0xa4],0x100` in CUnit::CUnit.
struct_fields.revises: the comment was the one word `bool`; it now says what reads it and that it is not upgrades alone. Name and type unchanged

struct_fields.name: upgrade_active
struct_fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are re-equipped, saved as `can_upgrade`. CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51CF82, 0x51D07A). **The constructor sets it**, so a unit upgrades unless told not to.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0xa5],0; je` in the upgrade body; `mov word ptr [edi+0xa4],0x100` in CUnit::CUnit writes 1 here.
struct_fields.revises: the comment was the one word `bool`. Name and type unchanged

struct_fields.name: reinforcements_active
struct_fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are brought back to strength, saved as `can_reinforce`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51BC42, 0x51BD26). **The constructor sets it.**
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [edi+0xa6],0; je` in the reinforcement body; `mov byte ptr [edi+0xa6],1` in CUnit::CUnit.
struct_fields.revises: the comment was the one word `bool`. Name and type unchanged

struct_fields.name: build_discount_extra
struct_fields.comment: thousandths, added to the technology category discount by CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount (0xE1AC0), its one reader - so it comes off the cost of every unit and off its build time alike. **What the technology key `ic_efficiency` adds up to**: the effect of `industral_efficiency`, 0.025 a level. That is measured, not read off a loader: with Germany's four levels two days of the upgrade share reproduce a savegame on all 1,469 of its technology lines, and without them none of its build times fit. The neighbour of ic_bonus at +0x90, which is `ic_modifier`, and not the same figure.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain --holder 0xDF8 --field 0x94 answers one reader, `add eax,[edx+0x94]` at 0x4E1BB8. The key is from the measurement in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 6; wrong if a country with levels of industral_efficiency ever builds at the undiscounted price.
struct_fields.revises: the comment said what reads it and not what fills it; the technology key is added, marked as measured. Name and type unchanged
